correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge4\), explicit open neighborhoods give exactly two 2m-facet covers XA and XB. In each cover, unique opposite-layer vertices can be collapsed onto the boundary of an (m-1)-simplex, so each is \(S^{m-2}\). Their intersection is exactly K_(m,m) minus a matching, connected with cycle rank \(m^2-3m+1\). Both inclusions from this 1-dimensional graph to the simply-connected side covers are nullhomotopic, and the homotopy pushout gives the exact sphere wedge. Purity and non-shellability follow from the facets and nonzero lower-degree homology. Reproducible independent mod-2 boundary ranks m=4..8 match all predicted Betti numbers, not used as the infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Graph and invariant must both coincide, not just the graph name or wedge keyword. An ordinary open neighborhood N(v) omits v; a closed neighborhood N[v] contains v. For m=4 the open complex has seven 2-spheres versus nine for the closed one, and for \(m\ge5\) the open complex has nonzero degree m-2 homology. These are not equivalent. Also neither cut nor matching complexes are open-neighborhood complexes.

originality.rationale: The exact open-neighborhood wedge is not a corollary of the inspected same-graph cut-complex classification (arXiv:2304.13675 Theorem 7.18), the closed-neighborhood classification (arXiv:2511.12608 Example 3.5), or Shukla's degree<=3/four-regular circulant open-neighborhood theorems (arXiv:1802.04526 Theorems 2.1–2.6). Matsushita's closed result for this same graph has \(\beta_2\)=(m-1)^2, whereas here \(\beta_2\)=\(m^2-3m+1\) for \(m\ge5\), with additional \(\beta_{m-2}\)=2. value.rationale: This is an exact natural unbounded-family homotopy classification of the Lovasz open-neighborhood complex for the named clique-prism Cartesian product. For \(m\ge5\) it has structurally unexpected mixed-degree homology (two high-dimensional spheres plus a quadratic number of degree-2 spheres), explicitly differs from the already classified closed-neighborhood complex of the identical graph, and proves non-shellability for every \(m\ge4\). These properties answer a natural missing graph invariant in the topological-combinatorics literature and provide reusable benchmarks rather than a narrow arbitrary enumeration.
